title: Screening self-peptides for recognition by mouse alloreactive CD8+ T cells
author: Son, Paul-Heng, et al.

steps.title: Prepare AAV vector dose
steps.instruction: Make single‑dose aliquots of the AAV stock in sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, store at –80 °C; each mouse receives 5 × 10¹¹ vgc. Before injection thaw an aliquot on ice, add 500 µL sterile PBS, keep on ice and draw the diluted dose immediately before injection.

steps.title: Generate MBL QuickSwitch tetramers
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL MBL QuickSwitch H‑2Kb tetramer into a microtube, add 1 µL peptide then 1 µL Peptide Exchange Factor with gentle mixing, incubate 4 h at 20 °C protected from light. Quantify exchange by capturing tetramers on beads and incubating with a FITC‑conjugated antibody against the exiting peptide.

steps.title: Generate BioLegend Flex‑T tetramers
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL diluted peptide (400 µM) and 20 µL Flex‑T monomer into a microtube, illuminate with 366 nm UV light for 30 min on ice, then incubate 30 min at 37 °C in the dark. Detect exchanged monomers with the LEGEND MAX™ Flex‑T™ Human Class I Peptide Exchange ELISA Kit. For tetramer assembly transfer 30 µL exchanged monomer to a new tube, add 3.3 µL PE‑Streptavidin (0.2 mg/mL), incubate 30 min at 4 °C protected from light. Prepare blocking solution by mixing 1.6 µL 50 mM D‑Biotin and 6 µL 10 % (w/v) sodium azide in 192.4 µL PBS; add 2.4 µL blocking solution to the tetramer mixture and incubate ≥16 h at 4 °C protected from light. For dextramers transfer 6 µL exchanged monomer, add 10 µL 160 nM Klickmer‑PE, incubate 30 min at 20 °C and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Isolate liver leukocytes (Day 7)
steps.instruction: At 7 days post‑inoculation anesthetise mouse with isoflurane 3 % and O₂ 0.6 L/min, perform midline laparotomy, expose inferior vena cava, insert a 22G cannula distal to the renal bifurcation and transect the hepatic portal vein. Perfuse liver with 20 mL PBS (20 °C) by manual injection over 1 min. Transect liver lobes, transfer to a 100 µm cell strainer, press through and wash with cold RPMI + 5 % FCS, collect slurry in a 50 mL tube. Wash twice with 50 mL RPMI/FCS5, centrifuge 400 × g 10 min each. Decant supernatant, resuspend pellet in 15 mL PBS, add 9 mL Isotonic Percoll PLUS, mix and centrifuge 500 × g 15 min (no brake). Discard supernatant, wash pellet 400 × g 10 min. Resuspend in 2 mL red‑cell lysis solution, incubate 2 min at 20 °C, then wash twice 400 × g 10 min with RPMI/FCS5 and count viable cells.

steps.title: Prepare dasatinib solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve dasatinib in sterile DMSO to 10 mM, aliquot and store at –80 °C (≤3 months). On staining day thaw an aliquot at 20 °C, dilute 10 µL of 10 mM stock in 2 mL PBS (1:200) to obtain 50 000 nM, then dilute 10 µL of this in 2 mL PBS (1:40 000) to obtain 250 nM; this 250 nM solution will be used for the 50 nM final incubation.

steps.title: Prepare antibody panel
steps.instruction: In cold staining buffer (2 % FCS in PBS) prepare the fluorophore‑conjugated antibody panel on the day of staining, ensuring the CD8 antibody is the KT‑15 clone.

steps.title: Tetramer and antibody staining
steps.instruction: Wash isolated cells once with staining buffer (400 × g 10 min). Resuspend 1 × 10⁶ cells in 40 µL staining buffer. Add 10 µL of 250 nM dasatinib to reach 50 nM final concentration and incubate 30 min at 20 °C. Meanwhile spin the pMHC tetramer at 16 000 × g 1 min to remove aggregates. Add 0.5 µg pMHC‑PE tetramer, incubate 30 min at 20 °C. Wash twice (400 × g 10 min). Incubate with mouse TruStain FcX (1 µL in 50 µL staining buffer) 10 min at 4 °C. Add 0.5 µg purified anti‑PE (1 µL in 50 µL staining buffer), incubate 30 min on ice. Wash twice (400 × g 10 min). Add surface antibodies (total 100 µL staining buffer per sample), incubate 30 min on ice. Wash twice with PBS (400 × g 10 min). Add viability dye ZNIR (total 100 µL PBS), incubate on ice 15 min. Wash twice with staining buffer (400 × g 10 min). Resuspend cells in 150 µL staining buffer, filter through a 50 µm nylon mesh, and proceed to flow cytometry analysis. Include FMO, unstained, and viability‑only controls; PD‑1‑negative bystander cells serve as internal negative controls.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for identification of immunogenic self-peptides presented by H-2Kb. For B10.BR recipients, we used 178.3 mice (Kb transgenic on a B10.BR background) as skin donors while for BALB/c recipients, the skin donors were C57BL/6 (H-2b) mice. We have also used this protocol to identify immunogenic peptides bound by H-2Kd. Here, we used isolated liver leukocytes after a prime-boost as the source of a highly enriched alloreactive population. Alternatively, infiltrating T cells from transplanted organs (e.g., heart, kidney) may be used if examination of tissue-specific peptides is desired. QuickSwitch Custom Tetramer Kits (MBL International) were utilized to generate multiple tetramers in order to screen an array of >100 pMHC epitopes. Several other commercially-available reagents enable peptide MHC exchange or loading (BioLegend Flex-T – UV-mediated exchange monomer, ImmunAware easYmer, TetramerShop Empty Loadable Tetramer, etc). In a preliminary evaluation, comparable results were obtained with different peptide-exchange methods (Figure 6). Chaperone-mediated peptide exchange is another recently-reported method that would be suitable for use with this protocol.2
